::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Febry 26th 1864  
**From:** Elderfield Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS British Library Add MSS 54920: 21-22
:::

My dear [Mr Macmillan](people/person_939.qmd),
I suppose [the Trial](cmy_books/cmybook_53.qmd) ought to be stereotyped that it may stand on the same footing with the other books. In all the former cases I have been at the whole expense of printing, paper, binding &c, and have thus had [all the profits](organizations/other_160.qmd), except the commission on the sales - I think the arrangement with regard to the Trial was that I was to receive £200 for 2,000 copies; I conclude therefore that the £68 would be separately my purchase of the stereotype plates - It makes a considerable diminution of the profits of the first edition, but it is certainly a necessary one and I agree to the arrangement.

I am glad you decided against [illustrations](organizations/other_167.qmd) for the [Little Duke](cmy_books/cmybook_20.qmd). [Mrs Blackburn](people/person_159.qmd)’s were not very successful, though she had been so kind about them that I should hardly have liked to put out others by a different hand without first giving her the option. Those to the [Lances of Lynwood](cmy_books/cmybook_23.qmd) are much better, but she is never really at home without animals as her subject.

I think I prefer [Golden Deeds](cmy_books/cmybook_51.qmd) to noble deeds, but that may be only because I have thought of the incidents by the former title, and besides it is a little more uncommon and vague - which last is a gain in a miscellaneous sort of collection, and gives a certain sense of freedom in gathering them. I have a delightful letter about them from [Mrs Macmillan](people/person_941.qmd) which I am going to answer at once.

There are some grand incidents in the [Indian Mutiny](organizations/other_134.qmd) such as [Lieutenant Willoughby](people/person_1904.qmd)’s destruction of the powder at Delhi, Dr Hay remaining with the sick at Benares, and a young officer’s escape carrying a little girl of 3 years old.[^1] But I never saw them but in the Times, and I suppose the only chance of getting the sight of them again would be in some library when I am in London again.

Yours faithfully
C. M. Yonge		

There are two chapters of the Trial still to come

---

[^1]: Black-edged paper.
[^2]: All three incidents are included in *A Book of Golden Deeds*.
